subject: Budget thresholds & cache/batching alignment — post-call recap
body:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@zennova.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Budget thresholds & cache/batching alignment — post-call recap

Hi Samir — thanks for the time today. Quick recap so we’re all aligned and we can move to a scoped pilot:  

Key pain points you shared:
- Token spend is the primary gating issue for your product team; current forecasts show token cost > 60% of your ML infra run-rate at 2M monthly queries.
- Latency targets for interactive flows (<= 300ms p95) are strict — you can tolerate modest batching for lower-priority batch jobs but not on core checkout flows.
- Ops team needs clear budget thresholds for a pilot (monthly cap) and an escalation path if token spend trend hits 80% of that cap.

Goals we agreed on:
1) Prove a pilot that reduces per-request token cost by ~30–45% using batching + prefix caching and a quantized model variant where acceptable.
2) Keep core interactive flows at p95 <= 300ms while redirecting non-critical requests to cost-optimized routing.
3) Produce a simple dashboard and weekly checkpoint showing token spend, effective latency, and projected monthly cost at current volume.

Initial technical levers discussed:
- Batching: group background enrichment calls into 200–500ms micro-batches to cut per-token GPU overhead for non-interactive flows.
- KV/prefix caching: exploit repeated user prompts for returning customers to avoid re-tokenizing large context windows.
- Model variants + quantization: route cold/batch traffic to a 4-bit quantized variant for high-throughput jobs.
- Smart routing rules: hard-gate priority traffic to low-latency pool; fallback to cost pool if budget gates are exceeded.

Budget / commercial constraints:
- Your procurement team indicated a soft monthly budget cap of $27k for the pilot phase (1 month). If we can show >30% cost reduction in that time, you’ll consider a 3-month committed pilot.
- You asked for an example SOW-level estimate for token spend and a simple conservative cap; attached is a worked token-econ spreadsheet with the assumptions we used.

Proposed next steps (owner / ETA):
- I’ll send a lean SOW + pilot milestones (scope, success metrics, rollback policy) by Monday. (owner: me)
- Ben to provide a quick pilot sizing note — estimated GPU / throughput profile and a rough monthly token spend projection under the optimized configuration. (owner: Ben Carter, due Tue noon)
- Soojin to confirm minimal security checklist items we’ll need for access (KMS, audit logs) and whether that needs a PO before we spin up private test capacity. (owner: Soojin Lee, due Tue EOD)

Attachments: redwood_token_econ_estimate.xlsx (worked example), pilot-sow-template.docx (SOW skeleton)

If that looks right, can you confirm the $27k pilot cap and we’ll circulate the SOW? Also please confirm the list of stakeholders (ops, procurement, and product) that should be on the brief.

Thanks again — I’ll loop Ben and Soojin in on the SOW thread so we can get commitments.

Best,
Priyom
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

----
From: Samir Patel <samir@zennova.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 16:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Budget thresholds & cache/batching alignment — post-call recap

Thanks Priyom — that summary is perfect. Confirming a few things:  
- $27k/month cap for the first month (PO will need to sign off but procurement gave a verbal okay to proceed to SOW).
- Priority flows: login / checkout / live support (must stay <300ms p95). Everything else can be routed to cost-optimized buckets.
- Key stakeholders: Me (product), Aisha Trivedi (ops) <aisha.trivedi@zennova.ai>, and procurement (procure@zennova.ai). Please include them in the next doc.

Two asks from our side:  
1) In the SOW can you include an explicit rollback policy and a clause that we won’t be charged for exceedances resulting from misconfiguration on Redwood’s side? We need the financial guardrail.
2) Can Ben put together two simple spend scenarios (conservative / upside) with token-per-request assumptions? That will help procurement sign the PO.

Happy to move forward once we get the SOW and the two scenarios.

—Samir
Head of Product, Zennova AI

----
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@zennova.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 18:47:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Budget thresholds & cache/batching alignment — post-call recap

Folks — forwarding Samir’s confirmation. Two concrete asks: 
1) Ben — can you produce conservative and upside spend scenarios (same template as the attached) with clear per-request token assumptions and the expected reduction from batching + caching? Pragmatic numbers are fine; procurement needs something to attach to a PO. Target: 3 slides + one spreadsheet by Tue noon.
2) Soojin — Samir asked for a rollback/charge-back clause if we misconfigure and cause overspend. Can you outline a short paragraph we can insert into the SOW? Also flag any security gating items that would prevent us spinning up the test capacity without a PO.

I’ll draft the SOW skeleton and include the rollback language you provide. Ben/Soojin — if you prefer a quick 20m sync tomorrow morning I can set it up.

Thanks — Priyom
